name: Tigecycline
executiveSummary: IV glycylcycline reserve. Adult: load **100 mg**, then **50 mg every 12 h** (severe: load **200 mg** → **100 mg q12h**). Pediatrics ≥8 years: **1.2 mg/kg** load and every 12 h (max 100/50 mg).
indications:
## Indications

- Complicated skin/soft-tissue and intra-abdominal infections when better alternatives are lacking.
- Off-label/reserved MDR use per ID.

## Precautions

- **Increased mortality** signal in bacteremia/sepsis in some analyses — not first-line in shock.
- Frequent nausea/vomiting. Rare pancreatitis. Avoid in pregnancy (tetracycline class).
- No *Pseudomonas* coverage; limited vs *Proteus/Morganella*.

> Y-site incompatible with amphotericin B (incl. lipid) and diazepam.

adulto.dose: Standard: load **100 mg IV**, then **50 mg every 12 h**. Intensified (ID): load **200 mg**, then **100 mg every 12 h**.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute 5 mL NS/D5W; dilute in 100 mL (200 mg load → 200 mL); infuse **30–60 min**. No IV push.
adulto.notes: Child-Pugh C: reduce maintenance to 25 mg q12h after 100 mg load (label).

pediatrico.dose: ≥8 years: load **1.2 mg/kg** (max **100 mg**), then **1.2 mg/kg every 12 h** (max **50 mg**/dose). ≥12 years and ≥40 kg: adult regimen may be used.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~24 h room temp.
- Diluted: up to ~48 h room temp (label).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, ↑ bilirubin, pancreatitis (rare), photosensitivity, *C. difficile*.
